newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco bans cephalopod fishing for four months.
newsitem.headline: Morocco bans cephalopod fishing for four months.

text.p: Morocco on Monday issued details on a ban on fishing for shrimp, cephalopods and similar species in Moroccan waters to give fish stocks time to develop.
The fishing and merchant marine ministry said in a statement, carried by the official Moroccan news agency MAP, that cephalopod fishing would be illegal in March and April, and September-October.
Shrimp fishing would not be allowed in January and February and there would be a ban on certain other species in February and March.
"The measures are to implement a fishing agreement between Morocco and the European Union reached at the end of joint committee meetings on January 9," it added.

The ministry also said that from the second year of the accord, which began on December 1, 1996, the number of European vessels allowed in the Moroccan waters would be cut to 552 units from the current 590 units.

After months of wrangling Morocco reached a four-year fisheries agreement with the European Union under which the EU pays the North African country $162.5 million a year in fees for fishing rights for the Spanish-dominated European fishing fleet.
